newsitem.title: UK: IMRO completes review of funds' unlisted holdings.
newsitem.headline: IMRO completes review of funds' unlisted holdings.

text.p: UK regulator IMRO said it has completed its review of the unlisted holdings of a sample of fund management groups, a planned follow-up to its recent report on UK unit trust managers.
A statement from the Investment Management Regulatory Organisation (IMRO) said the fund groups in its sample manage 46 percent of the 219 UK unit trusts identified as holding unquoted securities.
The review comes only weeks after IMRO investigations uncovered disproportionate holdings of unquoted securities in two funds managed by Morgan Grenfell Asset Management.
The funds were temporarily suspended and their managers later fired, while Morgan Grenfell's parent Deutsche Bank was obliged to stump up some 180 million stg to bale out the funds.
"As expected, the inspections confirmed that fund management groups hold minimal positions, if indeed any, in unquoted securities," IMRO said.

"The firms that do hold unquoted securities in their portfolios generally undertake an enhanced level of oversight of these securities and in the majority of cases, IMRO is satisfied with the controls."
But IMRO also noted the standard of some control processes, including documentary evidence, could be better.
It also said that although some firms rely on independent sources for the pricing of unquoted securities, some place "too great a reliance upon a single independent pricing source."
Improvement could also be made in the identification of unquoted securites and "the clarity of their disclosure in managers' reports and accounts."
IMRO said it was writing to certain firms with comments on their visits but did not anticipate further investigations.
The results of the inspection visits will be taken into account in IMRO's review of unit trust rules.
IMRO regulates 171 unit trust managers operating 1,677 authorised unit trusts and accounting for 10 percent (100 billion stg) of funds under management.
